Open-source research collective · Sri Lanka

Exposing Misinformation, Empowering Communities

Watchdog is an open-source research collective in Sri Lanka. We bring journalism, data science and technology together. Since 2019 we have hunted misinformation, investigated matters of public welfare, and built software tools, either to help the country work better or to help you understand how it can.

Discover by topic

All articles →
Special Reports In which we dive deep into footage to reconstruct the timeline of recent events with national implications. Expect photos, videos, maps. 20 stories Food & Agriculture In which we explore how food gets onto our plates, as well as the dangerous narratives and the disastrous policy decisions that led us to where we are today. 8 stories Healthcare In which we dissect critical healthcare issues and their impact on society, analyzing the systemic challenges and the path to a healthier future. 5 stories Transport In which we unravel the intricate web of transportation systems, uncovering the interplay between infrastructure, technology, and urban planning that shapes how we move and connect. 5 stories Electricity In which we illuminate the complex dynamics of the power sector, tracing the sources of energy, the evolution of grids, and the policies shaping the electrified world we inhabit. 2 stories Economy In which our resident economist explores the multi-decade reasons behind Sri Lanka’s default, examining trade, taxation and national income. 13 stories

Who we are

Watchdog began in April 2019, days after the Easter Sunday bombings, as a group of concerned citizens countering misinformation. Today we are journalists, researchers and software engineers publishing open data, open code and stories in three languages.
